summary: The root "Aff" primarily denotes a sound or expression of disgust, impatience, or contempt, often made by blowing or exhaling. It signifies a strong dislike or disapproval, as in saying "Uff!

headwords.gloss: dirty, a filthy, an unclean; in want; poor; possessing little; A coward

parts.t: signifying the “dirt of the nail.” (TA.) One
holding back, by reason of disgust,

headwords.def: أُفَّةٌ : see أُفٌّ , in four places. Also A dirty, a filthy, an unclean, man: (K:) from أُفٌّ signifying the “dirt of the nail.” (TA.) One in want; poor; possessing little: (K:) from أَفَفٌ signifying “a thing little in quantity.” (TA.) A coward: (K:) as though originally ُو أُفَّةٍ , i. e. holding back, by reason of disgust, ( مُتَأَفِّفٌ ,) from fight: (TA:) or experiencing vexation or disgust, and languid or sluggish, in war: (IAar:) also heavy, or sluggish. (IAth.)
إِفَّةٌ أفه افه افة فاه وفى آفة : see إِفَّانٌ in three places.
أَفَفٌ Vexation, distress of mind, or disgust. (T, IAth, K.) See also أُفٌّ , in three places. And see إِفَّانٌ , in three places.
أَفَهْ and أَفَّهٌ and أٌفَّهٌ and أُفِّهْ and أُفُّهْ : see أُفٌّ .
